title: Aph. XXIII: Apocalyptic part; Cap. 9 close
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss: they might acknowledge that same they stand as always Christ's care — but taught little by little by the experience belonging toward predicted events. the fourth part belonging toward the New Testament, written by the Apostle John concerning those things that same which Christ himself revealed about the state belonging toward the New Testament churches — from its beginning through seven distinct periods plus faces portrayed in the Ephesian, Smyrnaean, Pergamene, Thyatiran, Sardian, Philadelphian, plus Laodicean, unto the world's end — plus concerning their gifts, dangers, calamities, Antichrist's persecutions, deliverances, the last judgment, the dreadful damnation belonging toward the impious, plus the supreme glorification belonging toward the churches plus the godly in it — lest, ignorant belonging toward their own fates plus future lot, like Gentiles or brute beasts, they should be overwhelmed plus perish by sudden chances; — there remains the Apocalyptic. XXIII.
pass_b_english: XXIII. There remains the Apocalyptic, the fourth part of the New Testament, written by the Apostle John concerning those things which Christ himself revealed about the state of the New Testament churches — from its beginning through seven distinct periods and faces portrayed in the Ephesian, Smyrnaean, Pergamene, Thyatiran, Sardian, Philadelphian, and Laodicean, unto the world's end — and concerning their gifts, dangers, calamities, Antichrist's persecutions, deliverances, the last judgment, the dreadful damnation of the impious, and the supreme glorification of the churches and the godly in it — lest, ignorant of their own fates and future lot, like Gentiles or brute beasts, they should be overwhelmed and perish by sudden chances; but taught little by little by the experience of predicted events, they might acknowledge that they are always Christ's care.
source_text: XXIII. Superest Apocalyptica, quarta pars N.T., a Johanne Apostolo conscripta de iis, quae Christus ipse revelavit de statu ecclesiarum novi testamenti, ab illius initio per septem distinctas periodos & facies in Ephesina, Smyrnenfi, Pergamenfi, Thyatirenfi, Sardenfi, Philadelphenfi & Laodicena effigiatas usque ad finem mundi, deque earum donis, periculis, calamitatibus, Antichristi persecutionibus, liberationibus, extremo judicio, impiorum horrenda damnatione, ecclesiarum piorumque in ea summa glorificatione, ne fatorum suorum sortisque futurae ignari, instar gentilium aut brutorum, subitaneis casibus obruerentur ac perirent, sed eventuum praedictorum experimento paulatim docti agnoscerent, se Christo semper curae esse.
